item.title: Singapore Still Lets You Smoke in Some Bars, but Vaping Can Cost You $10,000
item.description: Singapore's contrasting treatment of smoking and vaping raises questions about the consistency of its nicotine regulations. While cigarettes remain permitted in designated smoking areas within some bars and clubs, possessing or using a vape can result in fines of up to S$10,000. (Published on November 23, 2026byloopliner.com)

item.title: Switching completely from smoking to vaping linked to up to 92% lower toxicant exposure, CoEHAR review finds
item.description: Switching completely from smoking to vaping is associated with reductions of up to 92% in exposure to harmful chemicals, according to a new systematic review and meta-analysis published inArchives of Toxicology. (Published on November 24, 2026bycoehar.org)

item.title: Kenya's Nicotine Pouch Ban Would Punish Smokers and Reward the Black Market
item.description: Kenya is considering legislation that could impose penalties of up to ten years in prison and a KSh 5 million fine for nicotine pouch use, while conventional cigarettes would remain legally available. (Published on November 24, 2026byprohibitiondoesnotwork.com)
